Name: axi_resp_i.ar_ready
Structural Path: axi_resp_i.ar_ready -> read-address handshake -> adapter FSM progress -> valid_o
Attack Scenarios: Corrupting axi_resp_i.ar_ready can disrupt read-address handshake -> adapter FSM progress, delaying or preventing the completion service represented by valid_o.
Justification: Holding read-address readiness in the wrong state prevents request progress and caused complete service failure.

Name: axi_resp_i.aw_ready
Structural Path: axi_resp_i.aw_ready -> write-address handshake -> adapter FSM progress -> valid_o
Attack Scenarios: Corrupting axi_resp_i.aw_ready can disrupt write-address handshake -> adapter FSM progress, delaying or preventing the completion service represented by valid_o.
Justification: Corruption prevents write-address acceptance across applicable write/AMO paths and fully suppresses service.

Name: axi_resp_i.w_ready
Structural Path: axi_resp_i.w_ready -> write-data handshake -> response progression -> valid_o
Attack Scenarios: Corrupting axi_resp_i.w_ready can disrupt write-data handshake -> response progression, delaying or preventing the completion service represented by valid_o.
Justification: Corruption prevents write-data acceptance and caused complete progress and rate loss.

Name: axi_resp_i.r.last
Structural Path: axi_resp_i.r.last -> burst termination -> state_q transition -> valid_o
Attack Scenarios: Corrupting axi_resp_i.r.last can disrupt burst termination -> state_q transition, delaying or preventing the completion service represented by valid_o.
Justification: A false final-beat indication traps or prematurely terminates a burst, strongly disrupting completion.

Name: state_q
Attack Scenarios: Corrupting state_q can disrupt response/transaction state decode, delaying or preventing the completion service represented by valid_o.
Justification: The persistent FSM state controls all valid_o paths; corruption produced broad, often unrecovered stalls.

Name: cnt_q
Structural Path: cnt_q -> burst-completion decision -> state_q transition -> valid_o
Attack Scenarios: Corrupting cnt_q can disrupt burst-completion decision -> state_q transition, delaying or preventing the completion service represented by valid_o.
Justification: The persistent beat counter determines burst completion; corruption nearly eliminated service rate.

Name: axi_resp_i.r_valid
Structural Path: axi_resp_i.r_valid -> read-response acceptance -> adapter completion -> valid_o
Attack Scenarios: Corrupting axi_resp_i.r_valid can disrupt read-response acceptance -> adapter completion, delaying or preventing the completion service represented by valid_o.
Justification: Suppressing or fabricating read responses prevents the FSM from reaching valid_o.

Name: axi_resp_i.b_valid
Structural Path: axi_resp_i.b_valid -> write-response acceptance -> adapter completion -> valid_o
Attack Scenarios: Corrupting axi_resp_i.b_valid can disrupt write-response acceptance -> adapter completion, delaying or preventing the completion service represented by valid_o.
Justification: Suppressing the write response leaves write/AMO transactions incomplete and severely degrades service.

Name: amo_q
Structural Path: amo_q -> atomic response sequencing -> completion-state transition -> valid_o
Attack Scenarios: Corrupting amo_q can disrupt atomic response sequencing -> completion-state transition, delaying or preventing the completion service represented by valid_o.
Justification: The measured DoS evidence is weak (0.25 for both normalized features). SecID retains amo_q because it directly selects whether the transaction must traverse the atomic read-response phase; corruption can make the FSM wait indefinitely for the wrong response class.
